typescript: With strictNullChecks enabled, what happens when you compile let s: string = null;?
A compile error: null is not assignable to string
It compiles and s becomes an empty string
It compiles but throws a TypeError at runtime
It compiles with a warning that can be ignored
Under strictNullChecks, null and undefined are separate types and must be included explicitly, for example string | null.
What type does TypeScript infer for x in const x = "hello";?
The literal type "hello"
The primitive type string
The top type unknown
The implicit type any
A const binding cannot be reassigned, so TypeScript keeps the narrow literal type. With let x = "hello" it would widen to string.
Which declaration lets function getLength<T>(x: T) safely read x.length?
function getLength<T extends { length: number }>(x: T)
function getLength<T implements { length: number }>(x: T)
function getLength<T: { length: number }>(x: T)
function getLength<T super { length: number }>(x: T)
Generic constraints use the extends keyword. TypeScript has no implements, colon or super syntax for type parameters.
Given type Box<T = string> = { value: T }; what is the type of b.value after let b: Box;?
string
unknown
any
never
T has a default type of string, so Box with no type argument is Box<string>.
In function f(x: string | number) { if (typeof x === "string") { return x.length; } return x; }, what is the type of x in the final return?
number
string | number
string
never
The typeof check narrows x to string inside the if block, and because that block returns, x is narrowed to number after it.
Given type A = { a: number }; type B = { b: string };, which object is assignable to A & B?
An intersection type requires all members of both types with their declared types, so the object needs a as a number and b as a string.
What does TypeScript reduce the type string & number to?
never
string | number
unknown
any
No value can be both a string and a number at the same time, so the intersection of these primitives is never.
You write interface User { name: string } and later interface User { age: number } in the same scope. What is the result?
One User interface with both name and age
A Duplicate identifier compile error
The second declaration replaces the first
Only the first declaration is used
Interfaces support declaration merging. Declaring a type alias twice with the same name is an error instead.
Which of these can a type alias express but an interface declaration cannot?
A union such as string | number
An object type with methods
Optional and readonly properties
A string index signature
An interface always describes an object shape. Unions of primitives require a type alias.
Given type P = { x: number; y: string }, what is keyof P?
number | string
keyof produces a union of the property names of a type, not of their value types.
Given const config = { port: 3000 }; what is type C = typeof config;?
{ port: number }
{ port: any }
{ readonly port: 3000 }
Type-level typeof reads the inferred type of the variable. Property values in a mutable object literal widen to number; as const would keep 3000 and add readonly.
Which built-in utility type is equivalent to type RO<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }?
Readonly<T>
Required<T>
Partial<T>
Record<keyof T, T>
This is a mapped type that adds the readonly modifier to every property, which is exactly how Readonly is defined.
What does the -? modifier do in the mapped type { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] }?
Removes optionality, making every property required
Makes every property optional, like Partial does
Removes the readonly modifier from every property
Removes properties whose type is undefined
A minus prefix removes a modifier, so -? strips the optional flag. This is how Required<T> is implemented.
Given type IsStr<T> = T extends string ? "yes" : "no";, what is IsStr<string | number>?
"yes" | "no"
"no"
"yes"
"yes" & "no"
Conditional types distribute over unions when the checked type is a naked type parameter, so each member is evaluated separately.
Given type R<T> = T extends (...args: any[]) => infer U ? U : never;, what is R<() => boolean>?
boolean
() => boolean
never
unknown
infer U captures the return type of the function type. This is how the built-in ReturnType works.
What is Omit<{ a: number; b: string; c: boolean }, "a">?
{ b: string; c: boolean }
{ a: number; c: boolean }
{ a?: number; b: string; c: boolean }
{ b?: string; c?: boolean }
Omit builds a type with all properties except the listed keys, so a is removed entirely rather than made optional.
Which tsconfig.json setting turns on strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny and the other strict family checks at once?
"strict": true
"noImplicitAny": true
"strictMode": "all"
"checkJs": true
strict is an umbrella flag that enables the whole strict family. strictMode is not a real option, and checkJs only type checks JavaScript files.
Which tsconfig.json flag makes the compiler type check without writing any JavaScript output files?
"noEmit": true
"skipLibCheck": true
"isolatedModules": true
"declaration": false
noEmit is common when a bundler such as Vite or esbuild does the actual transpiling. skipLibCheck only skips checking .d.ts files.
In TypeScript 5.0 and later, which tsconfig flag selects the older, non-standard decorator implementation used by frameworks such as Angular?
experimentalDecorators
emitDecoratorMetadata
useDefineForClassFields
legacyDecorators
Without experimentalDecorators, TypeScript 5.0+ uses standard ECMAScript decorators. emitDecoratorMetadata only adds metadata on top of the legacy mode.
What happens when you compile let v: unknown = "hi"; v.toUpperCase();?
A compile error: unknown must be narrowed first
It compiles and returns "HI" at runtime
It compiles but throws a TypeError when it runs
It compiles because unknown behaves like any
unknown is the type-safe counterpart of any: you must narrow it, for example with typeof v === "string", before using it.
javascript: What does this print? console.log(1); setTimeout(() => console.log(2), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(3)); console.log(4);
Synchronous code runs first. Then the microtask queue (the Promise callback) drains before the next macrotask (the timer).
Which callback is queued as a microtask in a browser?
Promise reactions and queueMicrotask use the microtask queue. Timers and DOM events are scheduled as tasks (macrotasks).
What does this print? for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { setTimeout(() => console.log(i)); }
var is function scoped, so all three closures share one i, which is 3 when the timers fire. Using let creates a new binding per iteration.
What does this print? for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { setTimeout(() => console.log(i)); }
let creates a fresh binding for each loop iteration, so each closure captures its own value of i.
Given function make() { let c = 0; return () => ++c; } const f = make(); f(); f();, what does a third call f() return?
The returned arrow function closes over c, which persists between calls and is incremented each time.
Given class Animal {} and class Dog extends Animal {}, what does Object.getPrototypeOf(Dog.prototype) return?
extends links Dog.prototype to Animal.prototype, forming the prototype chain used for method lookup.
In strict mode, what happens? const o = { n: 1, f() { return this.n; } }; const g = o.f; g();
Calling g as a plain function sets this to undefined in strict mode, so reading this.n throws. In sloppy mode it would return undefined.
Where does an arrow function get its this value from?
The object it is called on
The global object, such as window
The first argument passed to it
Arrow functions have no own this binding, so call, apply and bind cannot change it.
Given function f() { return this.x; } const b = f.bind({ x: 1 });, what does b.call({ x: 2 }) return?
A bound function permanently fixes this. A later call or apply cannot override it.
Given async function f() { return 5; }, what does f() return?
A Promise that rejects with the value 5
A Promise that resolves to undefined
An async function always returns a Promise. A returned value becomes the resolution value.
Which method waits for all input promises and resolves with their outcomes even when some of them reject?
Promise.all rejects as soon as one input rejects. allSettled always resolves with an array of { status, value | reason } objects.
What does this print? console.log(a); var a = 5;
The var declaration is hoisted and initialized to undefined. The assignment stays in place.
let and const are hoisted but stay uninitialized in the temporal dead zone until the declaration line runs.
In Node.js, which package.json field makes .js files load as ES modules?
With type set to module, .js files are treated as ESM. .cjs files remain CommonJS regardless.
Inside a Node.js ES module, which of these is not available by default?
__dirname and require exist only in CommonJS. In ESM you derive paths from import.meta.url (Node 20.11+ also offers import.meta.dirname).
What does this print? if (true) { var a = 1; let b = 2; } console.log(a, typeof b);
var ignores block scope, so a is visible. b is block scoped, and typeof on a name that is not declared in scope returns "undefined" without throwing.
Why is a WeakMap a good fit for storing extra data about DOM nodes?
Its keys do not prevent the nodes from being garbage collected
It iterates its entries faster than a Map
It can use strings as well as objects as keys
It copies each node so later changes do not affect it
WeakMap holds keys weakly. When a node is removed and unreferenced, its entry can be collected. WeakMap keys must be objects, not strings.
Which is the safe way to display untrusted user input as text inside an element?
textContent inserts plain text and never parses HTML, which prevents script injection. The other options parse markup.
Two objects reference each other, but nothing else references either one. What happens in a modern JavaScript engine?
They leak until the page reloads
Only one of them is collected
Modern engines use reachability based collection (mark and sweep), which handles cycles. Pure reference counting would leak them.
What is a after const { a = 1, b } = { a: undefined, b: 2 };?
Destructuring defaults apply when the value is undefined. A null value would not trigger the default.
ruby: You implement method_missing to support dynamic finders such as find_by_email. Which method should you also override so respond_to? reports them correctly?
Ruby's respond_to? calls respond_to_missing? for methods that are not defined. Overriding it keeps respond_to? and method objects consistent.
Which Module method defines a new instance method from a block at runtime?
define_method(:name) { |args| ... } creates a real method whose body is the block. attr_accessor only generates fixed getters and setters.
Object obj has a private method greet. Which call raises NoMethodError?
public_send respects visibility. send and __send__ bypass it, and inside instance_eval self is obj, so a private call is allowed.
What does p = proc { |a, b| [a, b] }; p.call(1) return?
Procs are lenient about arguments: missing ones become nil. A lambda with the same body would raise ArgumentError.
What does method m return? def m; [1, 2].each { |x| return x }; :done; end
return inside a block returns from the enclosing method, so m exits on the first iteration. In a lambda, return would only leave the lambda.
Which check is most idiomatic in Ruby when a method should accept any object that can be iterated?
Duck typing cares about what an object can do, not its class. Checking for each accepts arrays, hashes, sets and custom collections.
Given s = "hi"; def s.shout; upcase; end, which objects respond to shout?
Only the object referenced by s
def s.shout adds a singleton method to that one object's singleton class, not to String.
Where is a method defined with def self.build inside class Foo stored?
In the singleton class of Foo
In the Module class that all classes share
Class methods are singleton methods of the class object, so they live in Foo's singleton class (its eigenclass).
What does Class.superclass return in Ruby?
In Ruby's object model, Class inherits from Module, which inherits from Object and then BasicObject.
A module Greeting defines def greet; "hi"; end. What does extend do when you write class Foo; extend Greeting; end?
It makes greet a class method, called as Foo.greet
It makes greet an instance method of Foo
It copies greet into every subclass only
It raises an error because modules cannot be extended
extend adds the module's methods to the receiver's singleton class. include would add them as instance methods.
Given module M; end; class C; prepend M; end, what are the first two entries of C.ancestors?
prepend inserts the module before the class in the lookup chain, so M's methods can wrap C's methods and call super.
Which method must a class define to get <, <=, ==, > and between? by including Comparable?
Comparable builds all its operators from the spaceship method <=>. Enumerable, by contrast, needs each.
Given h = { "a" => 1 }, what does h[:a] return?
The string "a" and the symbol :a are different keys. Hash#[] returns nil for a missing key, while fetch would raise KeyError.
Which statement about Ruby symbols is correct?
Each symbol name maps to one immutable object
Symbols can be modified in place with <<
Two :name literals create two different objects
Symbols are a subclass of String
Every occurrence of :name refers to the same object, which is why symbols are cheap and common as hash keys. Symbol is not a String subclass.
After require "json", what type are the keys of the hash returned by JSON.parse('{"a": 1}')?
JSON.parse uses string keys by default. Pass symbolize_names: true to get symbol keys.
Which call returns [[1, 2], [3, 4]] for the array [1, 2, 3, 4]?
each_slice splits into consecutive chunks. each_cons gives overlapping windows: [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]].
In Rails, what does User.where(active: true) return?
An Array of User objects loaded right away
The first matching User record, or nil
A raw SQL string ready to be executed
where builds a chainable Relation. The query runs only when results are needed, for example on each, to_a or first.
In Rails, no user has id 999. What does User.find(999) do?
It returns nil without an error
It creates a new user with id 999
find raises when no record matches, which Rails turns into a 404. find_by(id: 999) would return nil instead.
A Rails page lists posts and calls post.comments.size for each one, producing one query per post. Which change fixes this N+1 problem?
includes preloads the association in a fixed number of queries. joins alone filters with SQL but does not load the comments into memory.
Custom exception classes in Ruby should usually inherit from which class?
A bare rescue (and rescue => e) catches StandardError and its subclasses. Inheriting directly from Exception means those rescues will miss it.
php: A file starts with declare(strict_types=1); and defines function f(int $x) {}. What happens on the call f("5")?
A TypeError is thrown
The string is converted to 5
A warning is shown and 0 is used
The call is silently skipped
Strict mode disables scalar type coercion for calls made from that file. Without it, the numeric string would be coerced to int 5.
What does the parameter type ?string accept in PHP?
A string or null
Only a non-empty string
Any scalar value
A string or false
The leading question mark makes a type nullable. It is shorthand for the union type string|null.
Code in namespace App; calls new DateTime() without a use statement. What happens?
PHP looks for App\DateTime and fails if it does not exist
PHP silently falls back to the global DateTime class
PHP creates an empty App\DateTime class
PHP treats the call as a function call
Unqualified class names resolve against the current namespace and never fall back to global. Use \DateTime or use DateTime;. Functions and constants do fall back.
Which statement lets you refer to App\Models\User as U in the current file?
use App\Models\User as U;
import App\Models\User as U;
namespace U = App\Models\User;
alias U = App\Models\User;
The use keyword imports and optionally aliases a class name. PHP has no import or alias keywords for this.
A class uses traits A and B, and both define log(). How do you choose A's version?
use A, B { A::log insteadof B; }
use A, B { A::log override B; }
use A, B { B::log extends A; }
use A, B { prefer A::log; }
The insteadof operator resolves trait method conflicts. You can still keep B's version under another name with B::log as logB.
What happens when you run new Loggable() where Loggable is a trait?
An Error, because traits cannot be instantiated
A new object that exposes all of the trait's methods
A new empty stdClass object with no methods
A deprecation notice, and then a new object
Traits are only for reuse inside classes through use. They cannot be instantiated on their own.
Which PDO code safely looks up a user by an email address typed into a form?
$pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?")->execute([$email])
$pdo->query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '$email'")
$pdo->query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = " . addslashes($email))
$pdo->exec("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" . trim($email) . "'")
A prepared statement sends the value separately from the SQL text, so input cannot change the query structure. Escaping by hand is fragile.
Can a PDO placeholder be used for a table name, as in SELECT * FROM ? WHERE id = ?
No, placeholders only stand for values
Yes, if you bind it with PDO::PARAM_STR
Yes, but only with named placeholders
Yes, with emulated prepares turned off
Identifiers such as table and column names cannot be bound. Validate them against an allowlist instead.
In PHP 8.0 and later, what is the default PDO error mode?
PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION
PDO::ERRMODE_SILENT
PDO::ERRMODE_WARNING
PDO::ERRMODE_STRICT
PHP 8.0 changed the default from silent to exception mode, so failed queries throw PDOException. ERRMODE_STRICT does not exist.
composer.json maps "App\\": "src/" under autoload psr-4. Which file should contain the class App\Http\HomeController?
src/Http/HomeController.php
src/App/Http/HomeController.php
app/http/homecontroller.php
src/HomeController.php
PSR-4 strips the mapped prefix App\ and turns the remaining namespace segments into folders under src/.
Which Composer command installs exactly the versions recorded in composer.lock?
composer install
composer update
composer require
composer dump-autoload
install reads the lock file for reproducible builds. update resolves new versions and rewrites the lock file.
What does OPcache store to speed up PHP?
Compiled script bytecode in shared memory
Rendered HTML responses for each page URL
Database query results keyed by the SQL text
Session data for each logged-in user
OPcache saves PHP from parsing and compiling scripts on every request. Caching responses or queries needs other tools.
Production has opcache.validate_timestamps=0. You deploy new PHP files. What happens?
The old code keeps running until OPcache is reset or PHP restarts
PHP notices the changed files on the very next request and recompiles them
PHP returns a 500 error until the cache rebuilds itself
OPcache disables itself because the files on disk changed
With timestamp validation off, OPcache never checks files for changes. Deploy scripts must reset the cache, for example by reloading PHP-FPM.
Right after a user logs in, which call helps prevent session fixation attacks?
session_regenerate_id(true)
session_write_close()
session_set_cookie_params(0)
session_cache_expire(30)
Regenerating issues a new session ID once privileges change, so an ID an attacker planted earlier becomes useless.
With PHP's default session settings, where is $_SESSION data stored?
In files on the server, keyed by the session ID
Inside the session cookie, encrypted in the browser
In the browser's localStorage for the site
In the query string of every request URL
The PHPSESSID cookie only carries the ID. The default files handler keeps the data on the server.
What does match("1") { 1 => "int", default => "other" } return?
It returns "other"
It returns "int"
It returns null
It throws an error
match compares with strict identity (===), so the string "1" does not equal the integer 1. switch would use loose comparison.
Given enum Suit: string { case Hearts = 'H'; }, what does Suit::tryFrom('X') return?
null
A ValueError
Suit::Hearts
false
tryFrom returns null for an unknown value, while from throws a ValueError. Backed enums were added in PHP 8.1.
Which syntax declares a native PHP 8 attribute on a controller method?
#[Route('/home')]
@Route('/home')
/** @Route('/home') */
[[Route('/home')]]
Native attributes use #[...]. Docblock annotations are just comments that libraries parse, not a language feature.
What does public function __construct(private LoggerInterface $logger) {} do in PHP 8?
It declares and sets a private $logger property
It declares a local variable that is lost after construction
It makes the constructor itself private, so new fails outside
It injects a logger from a global container automatically
Constructor property promotion declares and assigns the property in one step. Wiring the dependency is still up to the caller or DI container.
A PHP REST endpoint receives a JSON request body. Why is $_POST empty, and what reads the data?
$_POST only parses form bodies; read json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'))
$_POST is filled only over HTTPS; read $_REQUEST['json'] with json_decode() instead
$_POST needs session_start() first; call it at the top and then read $_POST as usual
$_POST is filled only for PUT requests; read the raw body from $_GET['body'] instead
PHP fills $_POST only for form encoded and multipart bodies. A JSON body must be read from php://input and decoded.
dart: With dart:async imported, what does this print? print('a'); Future(() => print('b')); scheduleMicrotask(() => print('c')); print('d');
a d c b
a b c d
a d b c
a c d b
Synchronous code runs first, then the microtask queue drains, then the event queue, where Future(() => ...) callbacks are scheduled.
How do two Dart isolates share data?
By passing messages through ports
By reading the same global variables
By locking a shared mutex
By sharing one heap with atomic fields
Each isolate has its own memory and event loop. They communicate only by sending messages, for example through SendPort and ReceivePort.
Parsing a very large JSON file freezes a Flutter app's UI. Which fix actually removes the jank?
Run the parsing in another isolate with Isolate.run or compute
Mark the parsing function as async and await its result
Wrap the parsing call in Future.delayed(Duration.zero)
Convert the parsing into a Stream that emits each decoded item later
async code still runs on the main isolate, so CPU heavy work blocks frames. A separate isolate does the work in parallel.
With sound null safety, what happens when you compile String? name; print(name.length);?
A compile error, because name might be null
It compiles and prints 0, the default length
It compiles and prints null for the length
It compiles and throws only if name is null
A nullable type cannot be dereferenced directly. Use name?.length, a null check, or the ! operator.
What happens when code reads a late String s; field before anything has been assigned to it?
A LateInitializationError is thrown at runtime
It returns an empty string as the default value
It returns null, like any unassigned variable
A compile error is reported at the read site
late moves the initialization check from compile time to runtime, so reading too early throws.
What does this Dart code print? int? x; x ??= 5; print(x);
It prints 5
It prints null
It prints 0
A compile error
A nullable local without an initializer starts as null, and ??= assigns only when the current value is null.
Which return type should you declare for a Dart function marked async whose body ends with return 42;?
Future<int>
int
Stream<int>
Iterable<int>
An async function always returns a Future. The value returned in the body becomes the value the Future completes with.
Which function body modifier lets a Dart function yield values that callers consume with await for?
async*
sync*
async
yield*
async* produces a Stream. sync* produces an Iterable, and yield* is a statement that forwards another stream or iterable.
A Dart Stream from a StreamController() is listened to a second time. What happens?
A StateError: the stream has already been listened to
The second listener receives every event again
The first listener is cancelled automatically
The second listener only gets events added later
StreamController() creates a single-subscription stream. Use StreamController.broadcast() or asBroadcastStream() for several listeners.
Which State method in Flutter runs exactly once, when the State object is inserted into the widget tree?
initState
build
didUpdateWidget
activate
initState is the place to create controllers and subscriptions. build can run many times, and activate can run again when the State is reinserted into the tree.
A StatefulWidget creates an AnimationController in initState. Where should controller.dispose() be called?
In the State's dispose method
In the State's build method
In the State's didUpdateWidget method
In the State's deactivate method
dispose runs when the State is removed permanently, which is the right moment to release controllers, streams and listeners.
In a Flutter State, after an await that may take a while, which property should you check before calling setState?
mounted
context.isActive
widget.isBuilt
isDisposed
If the widget was removed during the await, calling setState throws. if (!mounted) return; guards against that.
What does mixin Swimmer on Animal { } mean in Dart?
Swimmer can only be mixed into classes that are subtypes of Animal
Swimmer automatically extends every subclass of Animal in the program
Swimmer replaces Animal's methods in every class that uses it
Swimmer can be instantiated only through an Animal instance
The on clause restricts which classes can use the mixin and lets the mixin call Animal members, including through super.
Mixins A and B both define hello(). Which version runs for C().hello() when class C with A, B {}?
B's version, since B is applied last
A's version, since A is listed first
Both run, in order A then B
A compile error about the conflict
Mixins are applied left to right, each one a new superclass layer, so the last mixin listed overrides earlier ones.
Which kind of Dart constructor may return an existing cached instance instead of creating a new one?
A factory constructor
A const constructor
A named generative constructor
A redirecting constructor
A factory constructor is not required to create a new instance and can return a cached object or a subtype. Generative constructors always create one.
Given class Point { final int x, y; const Point(this.x, this.y); }, what does identical(const Point(1, 2), const Point(1, 2)) return?
It returns true
It returns false
A compile error
It depends on the platform
Constant expressions with equal arguments are canonicalized, so both refer to the same object.
Which requirement must a class meet to have a const constructor?
All of its instance fields must be final
It must not declare any methods at all
It must not have any named constructors
All of its fields must be declared static
A const constructor builds compile-time constants, so the object's state must be immutable. That requires final instance fields.
Given extension on String { bool get isBlank => trim().isEmpty; }, what happens with dynamic d = '  '; print(d.isBlank);?
It throws NoSuchMethodError at runtime
It prints true, since the string is blank
It prints false, since d holds two spaces
It is a compile error on the d.isBlank call
Extension members are resolved from the static type. With a dynamic receiver the extension is not applied, so the runtime lookup fails.
What does this Dart list literal evaluate to? var a = [1, 2]; var b = [0, ...a, if (false) 9, 3];
The spread operator inserts the elements of a, and a collection if with a false condition adds nothing.
In Dart, what is the static type of s after var s = {};?
Map<dynamic, dynamic>
Set<dynamic>
LinkedHashSet<dynamic>
Map<Object, Object>
An empty {} is a map literal. To create an empty set, write <String>{} or declare the type, as in Set<String> s = {}.
lua: In Lua, what does t[1] return after local t = {"a", "b", "c"}?
nil
An index error
Table constructors assign list items to integer keys starting at 1, which is the convention for Lua sequences.
What does #t return for local t = {10, 20, 30}?
The length operator returns the size of a sequence. It is only well defined when the table has no holes.
In Lua, given local x = "k"; local t = {}, how do t.x = 1 and t[x] = 1 differ?
t.x uses the key "x", while t[x] uses the key "k"
They are the same, both use the key "k"
They are the same, both use the key "x"
t.x creates a global variable, while t[x] creates a field
Dot syntax is sugar for a string key: t.x means t["x"]. Brackets evaluate the expression, here the variable x.
What does the Lua statement t.name = nil do when the field already exists?
It removes the key from the table
It stores nil as a real value under the key
It raises an error for the nil value
It sets the field to an empty string
Tables never store nil values. Assigning nil is how you delete a key.
For local t = {1, 2, nil, 4, x = 5}, why might ipairs(t) and pairs(t) visit different entries?
ipairs stops at the first nil, while pairs visits every key
ipairs visits keys in random order, while pairs is sorted
pairs skips string keys, while ipairs includes them
pairs stops at the first nil, while ipairs visits every key
ipairs walks integer keys 1, 2, 3 until it finds nil. pairs uses next and visits all keys in an unspecified order.
What does print(t.hi) show? local t = setmetatable({}, { __index = function(_, k) return k .. "!" end })
hi!
nil
hi
table: hi
__index runs when a key is absent from the table. Here the function builds a value from the missing key.
Which metamethod lets you write a + b for two tables that represent vectors?
__add
__plus
__concat
__call
Arithmetic operators look for metamethods such as __add, __sub and __mul. __concat handles .. and __call makes a table callable.
A table has an __index metamethod. Which function reads a key without triggering it?
rawget(t, k)
next(t, k)
select(k, t)
getmetatable(t)[k]
rawget performs a primitive table access that ignores metamethods. rawset does the same for writes.
In Lua, what is obj:move(5) equivalent to?
obj.move(obj, 5)
obj.move(5)
move(obj, 5)
obj.move(self, 5)
The colon syntax passes the receiver as the first argument, which the method receives as self.
What does the second call return? co = coroutine.create(function(a) local b = coroutine.yield(a + 1); return b * 2 end); coroutine.resume(co, 1); coroutine.resume(co, 5)
true, 10
true, 2
false, 10
true, 12
The first resume yields a + 1 = 2. The second resume makes yield return 5, so the function returns 10, and resume reports success with true.
What does coroutine.status(co) return after the coroutine's function has returned normally?
"dead"
"suspended"
"normal"
"finished"
A coroutine that finished or raised an error is dead and cannot be resumed. A coroutine that has not started or has yielded is suspended.
What does the last call print? function counter() local n = 0 return function() n = n + 1 return n end end; local a = counter(); local b = counter(); a(); a(); print(b())
Each call to counter creates a new local n, so a and b have independent upvalues.
What does this print in Lua? local x = 1; do local x = 2 end; print(x)
It prints 1
It prints 2
It prints nil
An error: x redeclared
The inner local x is scoped to the do ... end block and shadows the outer x only there.
Inside a function, you write count = 0 without the local keyword. What does Lua do?
It creates or updates a global variable
It creates a local variable of the function
It raises an undeclared variable error
It creates a field on the function
Names without local are globals, stored in the _ENV table (the global table _G by default). This is a common source of bugs.
Why do Lua programs often write local insert = table.insert before a hot loop?
Local access is faster than repeated global and field lookups
Global functions cannot be called inside loops
It makes table.insert run in a separate coroutine
It prevents the garbage collector from running during the loop
Locals live in VM registers, while table.insert requires a global lookup plus a field lookup every time.
How does C code exchange values with Lua through the Lua C API?
Through a virtual stack of Lua values
Through shared C global variables
Through JSON strings passed by value
Through a pipe between processes
Functions such as lua_pushnumber and lua_tostring push and read values on a stack owned by the lua_State.
A C function registered with Lua has the signature int f(lua_State *L). What does its int return value mean?
How many results it pushed onto the stack
An error code, where 0 means success
The number of arguments it received
The type of the first result
Lua takes that many values from the top of the stack as the function's results.
Which C API call runs a Lua function in protected mode, so that errors are caught instead of aborting?
lua_pcall
lua_call
lua_resume
luaL_checkstack
lua_pcall returns an error code and leaves the error message on the stack. lua_call propagates errors.
A Lua program calls require("util") in two different files. How many times does util.lua run?
Once; later calls reuse package.loaded
Once per calling file, so it runs twice
Every time require is called from any file
Never, until one of its fields is first used
require caches each module's return value in package.loaded and returns the cached value on later calls, so the file runs only once.
In Lua, which values are treated as false in an if condition?
Only nil and false
nil, false and 0
nil, false, 0 and ""
Only nil
Unlike C or JavaScript, 0 and "" are true in Lua.
perl: In Perl, after "2024-05" =~ /(\d+)-(\d+)/, what does $2 contain?
Each pair of parentheses creates a numbered capture. $1 holds the first group and $2 the second, as a string.
In Perl, what does $1 hold after "abcbc" =~ /a(.*)c/?
"bcb"
"bcbc"
"bc"
The greedy .* grabs as much as possible and backtracks only to the last c. The non-greedy /a(.*?)c/ would capture "b".
Which Perl statement replaces every "cat" in $s with "dog"?
$s =~ s/cat/dog/g;
$s =~ s/cat/dog/;
$s =~ tr/cat/dog/;
$s = s/cat/dog/g;
The g flag makes s/// replace all matches, not just the first. tr/// maps individual characters, and without =~ the substitution applies to $_.
In Perl, given my %h = (a => 1), which expression reads the value for key a?
$h{a}
%h{a}
@h{a}
$h[a]
A single hash element is a scalar, so it uses the $ sigil with curly braces. Square brackets index arrays.
In Perl, after $h{k} = undef;, what are exists $h{k} and defined $h{k}?
exists is true, defined is false
exists and defined are both true
exists and defined are both false
exists is false, defined is true
exists checks whether the key is present, while defined checks whether its value is not undef.
In Perl, given my @a = (10, 20, 30);, what is $#a?
$#a is the index of the last element. The element count is scalar(@a), which is 3.
In Perl, given my @a = (10, 20, 30);, what are $n and $first after my $n = @a; my ($first) = @a;?
$n is 3 and $first is 10
$n is 10 and $first is 10
$n is 3 and $first is 3
$n is 30 and $first is 10
Assigning an array to a scalar gives its length (scalar context). Parentheses on the left create list context, which takes the first element.
What does Perl print for print scalar reverse("hello");?
olleh
hello
h
In scalar context reverse concatenates its arguments and reverses the characters. Without scalar, print gives list context and reverses a one-element list, printing hello.
Which Perl line opens data.txt for reading and stops with the system error if that fails?
open(my $fh, '<', 'data.txt') or die "Cannot open: $!";
open(my $fh, '>', 'data.txt') or die "Cannot open: $!";
open(my $fh, '<', 'data.txt') || warn "Cannot open: $@";
open(my $fh, 'data.txt', '<') and die "Cannot open: $!";
The three-argument form with '<' reads, '>' truncates for writing. $! holds the OS error, while $@ holds eval errors.
In Perl, which open mode appends to log.txt without erasing its contents?
'>>' opens for appending. '>' truncates the file first, and '+<' opens an existing file for reading and writing.
Inside while (my $line = <$fh>) { ... } in Perl, what does chomp $line; do?
Removes the trailing newline
Removes all whitespace from the line
Removes the last character whatever it is
Splits the line into words
chomp removes a trailing input record separator (a newline by default). chop removes the last character unconditionally.
Which command line tool is commonly used to install Perl modules from CPAN?
cpanm
pip
gem
composer
cpanm (App::cpanminus) installs modules from CPAN with their dependencies. pip, gem and composer serve Python, Ruby and PHP.
Where does Perl look for the CPAN module JSON::PP when it runs use JSON::PP;?
A file JSON/PP.pm under one of the directories in @INC
A file JSON-PP.pl in the current directory only
A file JSON.PP.pm under the directories in $PATH
A file named PP.pm in the JSON environment variable
Package separators :: map to directory separators, and Perl searches the directories listed in @INC.
In Perl, given my @a = (1, 2, 3); my $r = \@a;, which expression returns 1?
The arrow dereferences an array reference. $r[0] would index a different array @r, and $$r{0} treats $r as a hash reference.
In Perl, what does ref([1, 2]) return?
"ARRAY"
"LIST"
"REF"
Square brackets create an anonymous array reference, and ref reports its type. Curly braces would give "HASH".
Given my %data = (list => [10, 20]);, which Perl expression returns 20?
$data{list}[1]
$data{list}{1}
@data{list}[1]
$data[list][1]
The hash value is an array reference. Between subscripts the arrow is optional, so $data{list}[1] means $data{list}->[1].
What does this Perl code print? our $x = 1; sub show { print $x } sub test { local $x = 2; show() } test();
It prints 2
It prints 1
A compile error
It prints nothing
local temporarily replaces the global's value until test returns, and show sees it. With my $x = 2 inside test, show would print 1.
Which Perl declaration creates a variable visible only inside the enclosing block or file?
my
our
local
use vars
my creates a lexical variable. our and use vars declare package globals, and local only saves and restores a global's value.
In a Perl subroutine, where do the arguments passed by the caller arrive?
In the array @_
In the scalar $_
In the hash %ARGV
In the array @ARGV
Arguments arrive in @_, often unpacked with my ($a, $b) = @_;. @ARGV holds the script's command line arguments.
A Perl sub is called as f(@a, @b). Why is it hard for f to tell where @a ends?
Both arrays are flattened into one list in @_
Only the first array is passed to the sub
Each array arrives as a separate string
Perl passes arrays by name, not by value
Perl flattens list arguments. Pass references, as in f(\@a, \@b), to keep the arrays separate.
bash: In Bash, what does $? hold right after a command finishes successfully?
true
$? is the exit status of the last command. By convention 0 means success and any nonzero value means failure.
In Bash, var="a b". Why does [ $var = "a b" ] fail while [[ $var = "a b" ]] works?
[ is a command, so unquoted $var splits into two words
[ does not support the = operator for strings at all
[[ ]] converts both sides to numbers before it compares them
[ only works on file tests, not on string comparisons
[ is an ordinary builtin, so its arguments undergo word splitting. [[ ]] is shell syntax and does not split unquoted variables. Quoting "$var" also fixes [.
What does this Bash line print? name=John; [[ $name == J* ]] && echo yes || echo no
yes
no
yes no
Nothing
Inside [[ ]], an unquoted right side of == is a glob pattern, so J* matches John. With [ ] the asterisk would be treated differently.
What does this Bash line print? [[ 10 < 9 ]] && echo yes || echo no
yes
no
yes no
Nothing
Inside [[ ]], < compares strings lexicographically, and "1" sorts before "9". For numbers use (( 10 < 9 )) or [[ 10 -lt 9 ]].
In Bash, with default options, what is $? after false | true?
A pipeline's status is the status of its last command. With set -o pipefail it would be 1 because false failed.
In Bash with default options, what does this print? count=0; printf 'a\nb\n' | while read -r l; do count=$((count+1)); done; echo $count
An error
Each part of a pipeline runs in a subshell, so the loop's changes to count are lost. Use done < file or process substitution instead.
What does this Bash loop print? for i in {1..3}; do echo -n "$i "; done
Brace expansion turns {1..3} into the words 1 2 3 before the loop runs.
In Bash, f="report.tar.gz". What does echo ${f%.*} print?
report.tar
report
report.tar.gz
tar.gz
% removes the shortest match of .* from the end. %% would remove the longest match and leave report.
In Bash, path="/var/log/app.log". Which expansion prints app.log?
${path%/*}
${path#*/}
## removes the longest prefix matching */, leaving the file name. ${path%/*} would give /var/log.
In Bash, NAME is unset. What does echo ${NAME:-guest} print, and does it change NAME?
It prints guest and leaves NAME unset
It prints guest and sets NAME to guest
It prints nothing and sets NAME
It prints an error and exits
:- substitutes a default without assigning it. ${NAME:=guest} would also assign the value.
In Bash, what does this print? x=1; (x=2); echo $x
An empty line
An error
Parentheses run the commands in a subshell, a child copy of the shell. Variable changes there do not affect the parent.
A Bash script runs (cd /tmp && ls) and then pwd. What does pwd print?
The directory the script was in before
/tmp, where the subshell changed to
The home directory of the user
The filesystem root directory /
The cd happens only inside the subshell. Grouping with { ...; } instead would change the current shell's directory.
Which Bash line removes a temporary file however the script exits, including on errors with set -e?
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' KILL
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' ERR STOP
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' DEBUG
The EXIT trap runs when the shell exits for any reason it can handle. KILL and STOP cannot be trapped at all.
Which signal can a Bash trap never catch?
SIGKILL
SIGTERM
SIGINT
SIGHUP
SIGKILL (and SIGSTOP) are handled by the kernel and cannot be caught or ignored. kill without options sends SIGTERM, which can be trapped.
In Bash, which command sends both stdout and stderr of cmd to out.log?
cmd > out.log 2>&1
cmd 2>&1 > out.log
cmd 2> out.log 1>&3
cmd >> out.log 2>1
Redirections apply left to right. 2>&1 > out.log duplicates stderr to the old stdout (the terminal) before stdout moves. 2>1 writes to a file named 1.
In Bash, what is the difference between echo hi > f.txt and echo hi >> f.txt?
> truncates f.txt first, while >> appends to it
> appends to f.txt, while >> truncates it
> writes stdout, while >> writes stderr
> fails if f.txt exists, while >> creates it
Single > overwrites the file. Failing on an existing file only happens with set -o noclobber.
In Bash, after arr=(a b c), what does echo ${arr[1]} print?
b
a
c
a b c
Indexed arrays start at 0. Plain $arr refers to the first element, and "${arr[@]}" expands to all elements.
In Bash, after arr=(a b c); arr+=(d), what does echo ${#arr[@]} print?
+=( ) appends elements, and ${#arr[@]} gives the number of elements. ${#arr} would give the length of the first element.
A Bash script is run as ./s.sh "a b" c. How many words does for x in "$@"; do echo $x; done loop over?
"$@" expands to each argument as a separate word, keeping spaces inside arguments. Unquoted $@ or $* would split "a b" into two words.
A Bash script is run as ./s.sh one two three. What does echo $# print in it?
one
two
$# is the number of positional arguments, not counting $0 (the script name).
powershell: Which naming pattern do built-in PowerShell cmdlets follow?
Cmdlets use an approved verb plus a singular noun. Get-Verb lists the approved verbs.
Which cmdlet shows the properties and methods of the objects coming down a PowerShell pipeline?
Piping to Get-Member (alias gm) lists the object's type, properties and methods. Get-Command finds commands, Get-Help shows documentation.
In Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.CPU -gt 100 }, what does $_ refer to?
The current process object in the pipeline
The text line printed by Get-Process
PowerShell pipes .NET objects, not text. $_ (also $PSItem) is the current object, so its properties can be read directly.
Which PowerShell pipeline returns the five processes using the most CPU time?
Sort first, then take the first five. Selecting before sorting only sorts five arbitrary processes.
What does adding -WhatIf to Get-Service spooler | Stop-Service do?
Shows what would be stopped without stopping it
Stops the service and logs each step
Asks for confirmation before stopping it
Stops the service only if it is idle
-WhatIf describes the action without performing it. -Confirm is the parameter that prompts before acting.
What does this PowerShell script output? $x = 1; function f { $x = 2 }; f; $x
Assigning inside a function creates a variable in the function's local scope. To change the outer one, use a scope modifier such as $script:x.
How do you read the PATH environment variable in PowerShell?
Environment variables are exposed through the env: drive, so $env:NAME reads them. %PATH% is cmd.exe syntax.
Which operator tests whether $a is greater than $b in PowerShell?
PowerShell uses -gt, -lt, -eq and similar operators. > is the output redirection operator, so $a > $b writes to a file named after $b.
What is the default PowerShell execution policy on Windows client editions such as Windows 10 and 11?
Restricted allows interactive commands but no script files. Windows Server defaults to RemoteSigned.
What does the RemoteSigned execution policy allow?
Local scripts run; downloaded scripts need a trusted signature
Only scripts signed by Microsoft itself are allowed to run
All scripts run, but downloaded ones show a warning first
Scripts run only when they are sent through PowerShell remoting sessions
Files marked as coming from the internet must be signed by a trusted publisher. Unblock-File removes that mark from a file you trust.
Which statement about PowerShell execution policies is correct?
They are a safety feature, not a security boundary
They block all malicious code from running on the machine
They can only be changed by domain admins
They apply to cmd.exe batch files as well
Microsoft documents that execution policy prevents accidental script execution but is easy to bypass, for example by pasting the code.
Which command runs a script block on servers web01 and web02 over PowerShell remoting?
Invoke-Command fans out to many computers. Enter-PSSession opens an interactive session with a single computer.
Which default TCP port does WinRM use for PowerShell remoting over HTTP?
WinRM listens on 5985 for HTTP and 5986 for HTTPS. 3389 is RDP and 22 is SSH.
Which cmdlet configures a Windows computer to accept PowerShell remoting connections?
Enable-PSRemoting starts WinRM, creates listeners and session configurations, and adds firewall rules.
What does this PowerShell switch output? switch (3) { 1 { "one" } 3 { "three" } default { "other" } }
switch runs the block of each matching clause. default runs only when no clause matched.
Inside try { }, Get-Item C:\missing.txt fails, but catch never runs. What fixes it?
Add a finally block after catch
Most cmdlet failures are non-terminating errors, which try/catch ignores. -ErrorAction Stop turns them into terminating errors.
Which command installs a module from the PowerShell Gallery for the current user only?
Install-Module downloads and installs from a repository. Import-Module only loads a module that is already installed.
In a script module (.psm1), which cmdlet limits the functions that importers can see?
Export-ModuleMember chooses which functions, variables and aliases are public. A manifest can also restrict this with FunctionsToExport.
Get-ADUser -Identity jdoe does not show the LastLogonDate value. How do you include it?
Get-ADUser returns a small default set of attributes. Other attributes must be requested with -Properties.
Which ActiveDirectory module command finds user accounts that are currently locked out?
Search-ADAccount supports switches such as -LockedOut, -AccountDisabled and -PasswordExpired. Unlock-ADAccount unlocks a user.
webassembly: How are .wasm and .wat files related?
.wasm is the binary format and .wat is its readable text format
.wat is compiled machine code and .wasm is its source
.wasm runs in browsers and .wat runs only on servers
.wat is a JavaScript wrapper that loads .wasm
Both describe the same module. Tools such as wat2wasm and wasm2wat from WABT convert between them.
What does the WAT expression (i32.add (i32.const 2) (i32.const 3)) evaluate to?
The i32 value 5
The i32 value 23
The f32 value 5.0
A validation error
WebAssembly is a stack machine. The two constants are pushed, and i32.add pops both and pushes their sum.
Which is not one of the four core numeric value types of WebAssembly 1.0?
i8
The core numeric types are i32, i64, f32 and f64. 8-bit and 16-bit values exist only as memory load and store widths.
Which four bytes start every binary WebAssembly module?
WASM (0x57 0x41 0x53 0x4D)
\x7FELF (0x7F 0x45 0x4C 0x46)
The magic number \0asm is followed by a 4-byte version. \x7FELF is the Linux executable header and PK starts ZIP files.
Which toolchain is most commonly used to compile C and C++ to WebAssembly together with JavaScript glue code?
Emscripten
wasm-pack
AssemblyScript
Cargo
Emscripten (emcc) compiles C/C++ through LLVM and generates glue code. wasm-pack and Cargo are Rust tools, AssemblyScript is a TypeScript-like language.
Which Rust crate generates the JavaScript bindings that let Wasm functions take and return strings and JS objects?
wasm-bindgen
bindgen
cbindgen
wasm-encoder
wasm-bindgen generates glue on both sides of the boundary. The similarly named bindgen generates Rust bindings for C headers, and cbindgen generates C headers from Rust.
Which Rust compilation target produces Wasm for browsers with no assumed host system interface?
wasm32-unknown-unknown
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
wasm64-browser-js
asmjs-unknown-web
wasm32-unknown-unknown makes no assumptions about the host. wasm-pack uses it when building for the web.
How is WebAssembly linear memory organized?
As a contiguous, resizable array of bytes
As a garbage collected object heap
As separate memory for each function
As a key-value store of variables
Linear memory is a flat byte array addressed by integer offsets. In JavaScript it appears as an ArrayBuffer.
What is the size of one WebAssembly memory page?
64 KiB
4 KiB
1 MiB
16 KiB
memory.grow and the memory limits are counted in 64 KiB pages.
JS code created const view = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer). The module then grows its memory. What happens to view?
It is detached and must be recreated
It grows automatically with the memory
It still covers the old size and stays valid
It now points at the newly added pages only
Growing a non-shared memory detaches the old ArrayBuffer. Create a new view from memory.buffer after any call that may grow memory.
How is a JavaScript string usually passed to a Wasm function exported from compiled C code?
Encoded into linear memory, then passed as a pointer and length
Passed directly as a string parameter type in the function signature
Passed as a raw pointer into the JS engine's own string heap
Passed by packing all its characters into a single i64 value
Core Wasm functions take only numbers and references. Glue code encodes the text, often as UTF-8, into linear memory and passes its offset.
A module was loaded with WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes, imports). Where do you find its exported add function?
result.instance.exports.add
result.module.add
result.exports.add
WebAssembly.exports.add
instantiate with bytes resolves to { module, instance }. Exported functions, memories and tables live on instance.exports.
What is the importObject argument of WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(url), importObject) for?
Supplying JS functions and values the module declares as imports
Listing which of the module's exports should be made public
Configuring the fetch request headers and credentials for the .wasm file
Choosing the compiler optimization level for the module code
Wasm cannot call the host on its own. Everything it needs from outside, such as a log function or memory, is passed in as imports.
WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming fails with a type error, while fetching the file works. What is the most likely cause?
The server does not send Content-Type: application/wasm
The file is larger than one 64 KiB memory page of data
The module has no exported functions for JavaScript to call
The page loads the script without type=module set on it
Streaming compilation requires the application/wasm MIME type. Fix the server configuration or fall back to instantiate with an ArrayBuffer.
A Wasm function reads an address beyond the end of its linear memory. What happens?
It traps, and JS sees a WebAssembly.RuntimeError
It reads bytes from the browser's own process memory
It returns 0 silently and execution continues
The memory grows automatically to fit the address
Every memory access is bounds checked against the module's own memory, so a bad access stops execution instead of touching the host.
How can a WebAssembly module running in a browser modify the page's DOM?
Only by calling imported JavaScript functions
Directly, through built-in DOM instructions
Through a raw pointer into the browser's DOM tree
Through direct calls to the operating system
Wasm is sandboxed and has no direct access to browser APIs. It can only use capabilities the host passes in as imports.
C code with a buffer overflow is compiled to WebAssembly. What can the overflow still corrupt?
Data inside the module's own linear memory
Memory belonging to other browser tabs
The browser's JavaScript engine heap
Nothing, because Wasm checks all array bounds
Wasm keeps the bug inside the sandbox, but bounds are checked only against the whole linear memory, so neighboring C data can still be overwritten.
Which Content Security Policy source keyword allows WebAssembly compilation without allowing JavaScript eval?
'wasm-unsafe-eval'
'unsafe-eval'
'unsafe-inline'
'strict-dynamic'
'wasm-unsafe-eval' permits compiling Wasm only. 'unsafe-eval' would also allow eval and new Function.
For which task is moving code from JavaScript to WebAssembly most likely to give a big speedup?
Compute-heavy work like image filtering on large buffers
Frequent small DOM updates such as toggling CSS classes on nodes
Waiting on many network requests to finish in parallel
Reading many small values from localStorage in a loop
Wasm shines at tight numeric loops over memory. DOM work and I/O still go through JS APIs, and frequent boundary calls add overhead.
A Wasm function exported to JavaScript has an i64 parameter. Which JavaScript type must you pass?
BigInt
Number
String
Float64Array
The JS API maps i64 to BigInt so 64-bit integers keep full precision. Passing a regular Number throws a TypeError.
